set.body:
Raised by independent review. Observed since the first pass, filed now because it has persisted and Epic 9 will repeat it.

State

  HEAD = b5d9a33 "Certify the effectagram 0.1 foundation"
  16 untracked R files, 26 untracked test files, 14 tracked-and-modified R files.

HEAD does NOT contain the code the certification report describes. Verified with git cat-file:
  R/measurement.R    NOT in HEAD
  R/tomography.R     NOT in HEAD
also untracked: bridge.R, coupling-views.R, evidence-api.R, evidence-task.R,
measurement-decomposition.R, measurement-kernel.R, measurement-result.R,
measurement-storage.R, operations.R, pair-query.R - plus everything built this session:
geometry-plan.R, metric.R, relation-fit.R, support-index.R.

Consequences

1. The certified artifact SHA-256 in certification-report.md is computed over a working tree that
   was never committed. It is not recoverable or reproducible by anyone, including its author.
   A certification whose subject cannot be retrieved does not establish anything durable.

2. Epic 9 is "close the statistical 0.1 gate" and will produce a second, stronger certification
   covering crossnobis, metric construction, and the vertical slice. On the current tree it would
   inherit exactly the same defect, with more at stake.

3. Concrete data-loss exposure. A stray git clean -fd, a checkout, or a worktree switch destroys
   42 untracked files - the complete output of Epics 1, 2 and 3 - with no recovery point. That is
   the support index, the metric module with the sqrt_weight_congruence composition, and
   relation_fit, all of which I verified against base R this session and none of which exist in git.

4. Every reservation in this umbrella names paths that are untracked, so mote reservations are
   protecting files that version control does not know about.

This also interacts with Epic 0A. bd-01KZXEVFW3X074685EXWJZNP2D notes that the dead-export
question is about what is reachable; deleting exports is only safely reversible if the
pre-deletion state is committed. As of now it is not.

Suggested action, cheap and immediate

- Commit the current tree before Epic 4 lands, even as a work-in-progress commit. The point is a
  recovery point, not a clean history.
- Make Epic 9 acceptance require that the certified artifact correspond to a specific commit hash,
  and record that hash in certification-report.md alongside the content SHA.
- Consider whether the existing certification-report.md SHA claim should be withdrawn or annotated
  until it names a commit.

Not a code defect. It is a provenance defect in a package whose central claim is that every
reported value is traceable to its assumptions and provenance.
set.title: Certified artifact and all Epic 1-4 work exist only in an uncommitted working tree
